summary: This article explains what a fever is, how the brain raises body temperature to help fight germs, why we shiver and sweat, and how to care for someone with a fever.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “What Is a Fever?”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: how hot or cold something is
the parts of your body that work together to fight germs
a sickness caused by germs that get into the body

challengeTerms.def: a small part of the brain that controls body temperature, hunger, and thirst
a device that keeps a room or machine at a chosen temperature

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a fever is always a bad thing? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a fever helps the body fight an infection.
struggling: Pre-teach temperature, immune system, and infection with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use hypothalamus, thermostat, and multiply in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
